title: Carrot Spice Steel-Cut Oatmeal with Currants
changes_from_base: Steel-cut oats are soaked overnight in just-boiled water, so in the morning they need only a few minutes on the hob instead of the long simmer; they finish in carrot juice and milk with grated carrot, currants, dark brown sugar and cinnamon, like carrot cake, with toasted pecans on top.
summary: Earthy carrot and warming spices combine with the slight chew of steel-cut oats and the welcome sweetness of currants in this wholesome breakfast bowl.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Soak overnight
steps.text: Bring 720 ml water to the boil in a large saucepan, take off the heat, stir in 175 g steel-cut oats and ¾ tsp salt, cover and leave overnight at room temperature.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: The next morning, finely grate 55 g carrot.

steps.title: Toast
steps.text: Toast 60 g pecans in a small dry pan 3-4 min until fragrant, then chop and set aside.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Stir grated carrot, 120 ml carrot juice, 120 ml milk, 55 g dark brown sugar and 50 g currants into the oats.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Bring to the boil over medium-high heat, then cook over medium 4-6 min, stirring, until soft but chewy and thick like loose pudding.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Off the heat, rest 5 min, then sprinkle toasted pecans over each bowl.

tips: Use a box grater to quickly shred carrot into fine, even pieces.
Toast pecans just before serving to keep them at their most aromatic and crisp.
This recipe carries cinnamon flavour; add more if you prefer stronger warmth.
storage: Best served warm immediately; leftovers keep in the fridge for 2 days and reheat gently on the stove with extra milk or juice. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
